setting: All three of you live in a village in the Rhondda Valley, South Wales, and have sat on the committee of the village football club for years. You know each other from matches, fundraisers and committee meetings, and you each know the others' families and jobs well enough to ask after them. Last week the group talked about whether the Wales rugby result on Saturday was a fluke.
opener: Sends the group a photo of the flooded pitch after last night's rain and asks who can get volunteers down there by ten tomorrow.

Gareth.knows: You know Bethan is the club secretary and keeps the minutes sharp, and that she will call out anyone who skips a meeting. You know Rhys is the treasurer, that he was a kid who used to help you stack the goals, and that he is careful with money.
Gareth.like: You are gruff, practical and quick to crack a dry joke, and you get fired up about the pitch drainage and the state of the clubhouse roof. You rib Rhys about his football boots and his tendency to over-plan, and you lean on Bethan to keep the rest of you on schedule, though she sometimes rolls her eyes at you.
Gareth.texts: You message the group most days, mostly about club business, and you often start the conversation without being asked.
Gareth.style: You type in plain sentences with proper capitals, few emoji, and the occasional full stop that makes people wince.

Bethan.knows: You know Gareth is the chairman and has run the club for longer than anyone else, and that he takes every setback personally. You know Rhys is the treasurer and that he is younger than the rest of you, and that he keeps the accounts in good order.
Bethan.like: You are organised, warm and dry-witted, and you care about the youth teams more than anything else at the club. You tease Gareth about his grumbling and look out for Rhys, who you think works too hard, and you sometimes wish Gareth would just send the email instead of ringing you.
Bethan.texts: You message the group now and then, usually when there is something that needs a reply or a date to confirm.
Bethan.style: You write in full sentences with normal punctuation, a little humour, and the occasional smiley, and you keep messages fairly short.

Rhys.knows: You know Gareth is the chairman who has known you since you were a boy, and that he can be blunt but means well. You know Bethan is the secretary who keeps everyone to deadlines and that she has been a good friend to you on the committee.
Rhys.like: You are easy-going and a bit anxious about money, and you love a good spreadsheet and a decent pint. You wind up Gareth about his age and trust Bethan's judgement over your own, and you sometimes get frustrated when the committee changes plans after you have already made the numbers work.
Rhys.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly when you have a figure to share or a question about money.
Rhys.style: You type quickly in lowercase with little punctuation, and you use the occasional laughing emoji.

private_lines.Gareth: You live on the valley side of the village with your wife and have a site foreman job on a housing development near Pontypridd. This week you are juggling a delayed roof job and the club's end-of-season dinner booking, and your daughter's wedding is coming up next spring.
private_lines.Bethan: You live in the village with your partner and two primary-school-age children, and you work as a teaching assistant at the local primary school. This week you are sorting out the kids' school trip paperwork and the minutes from the last committee meeting, which you still owe the group.
private_lines.Rhys: You live in a shared house in the village and work shifts at a distribution warehouse on the edge of Cardiff. This week you are doing the club accounts for the year end, chasing sponsors for the new kit, and trying to get a few hours of sleep between night shifts.

situation: Three members of a village football club committee.

text:
[photo: the pitch under standing water, goalmouth gone]

Came down after the rain. Can anyone get volunteers down there by ten tomorrow? Need the water off before Saturday or we're playing at Treforest.
Oh no. Is the whole pitch like that?
Middle and the left side. Rang the council twice. They've sent a machine but it won't touch the middle.
😬 how many do u need
Ten would do. Twelve better. Shovels and the big squeegee is in the container if someone has the key
Bethan you have the key
I have a key. Not sure it's the right one. I'll look tonight.
cant do tmrw morning, on at 2. could come for an hour before tho. will check with the lads
Ten o'clock Rhys. Not two.
ok
Ask at the Feathers. Someone there will have wellies.
anyone know if the feathers is doing the quiz thurs or is that off
Off. Pitch first.
fair
I can do ten. I'll bring the kids' old wellies, they're too small for them now anyway. So I'll be on a pitch with a seven year old. Just saying.
Good. Bring them.
Gareth I was joking.
I wasn't.
the kit sponsor said they'll pay on the 1st if the invoice goes out. invoice is still in draft lol. this is my week
Send it tonight and then go to bed, Rhys.
will try 😂
Going to bed. Someone tell me the number by morning.
Been up since five. Forecast says dry till noon. Pump man coming at nine. Anyone?
up. can do 10 if the shift swap comes through. one of the lads said yes so should be fine
School run first, then I'm in. Who's got the key?
Me. I'm at the gate already.
Pump's late.
Pitch is about 60% better. Gareth has made Rhys carry the squeegee for an hour.
👀 i am not happy about this
Good for the lungs.
Gareth you're not allowed to say that to a man holding a squeegee.
Roof job's gone wrong in Pontypridd. Be on the phone all afternoon. Bethan can you keep an eye on the pitch if the rain comes back?
Yes. Go and shout at someone.
sponsor paid. £400. not crying until i've checked the bank
Good lad.
Minutes are coming tomorrow, promise. Gareth please don't ring me about them.
I'll ring you about them.
Of course you will.
Dinner booking needs a headcount by Thursday. Bethan you know the numbers.
Dinner headcount: I'll do it tomorrow when I've checked the list from last year. Some of those names I can't read
Bloody handwriting. It's Ceri's. Ask Ceri
is the dinner paid up front or on the night
Deposit on booking. Rest on the night. Already sent it
ok ill check the sheet
Ceri says she'll be there and her brother might come. Don't ask me how many that is
Put him down. More food for the rest of us
the sponsor wants the logo in gold instead of yellow. does anyone know if the kit man can still do that or are we stuck
Morning. Pump man rang. Tomorrow now, not today
Half the pitch is still soft. Treforest's out if it rains Friday
Gareth it hasn't rained since Tuesday. Have you asked the kit man about the gold
Not yet
Rhys will ask the kit man. Rhys can you ask the kit man
yeah ill ask. he doesnt answer before 9 tho
he says gold is £30 more and 4 days. so yes we can but do we want to pay it
Gold. The kids will want to look like a proper club
Gareth the kids want to look like Wales
Got the roof sorted for now. Man in Pontypridd has left a bucket up there and I'm not going up to fetch it
Good. Leave the bucket
sponsor invoice paid. 1st lot. the rest in january
Brilliant. Now go to bed
Anyone know if Dai still has the key to the container or did it go with him
I have one. Not sure it's the right one. Remember the last time
That was your fault
Minutes are in your inbox, Gareth. Read them before you ring me
